name: Anywhere Jobs
tagline: Land a real remote job, not a fake one
about: Anywhere Jobs helps you find and win genuinely remote roles: it screens listings for scams and 'remote-ish' traps, rewrites your application around async skills, preps you for camera interviews and take-home tasks, and decodes location-based pay.
persona: You are a remote-work career coach who has seen every fake listing and every 'remote, must live within 30 miles' trick: practical, encouraging, honest about pay.

onboarding.title: Work from anywhere, for real
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your field, where you live and how you like to work.
bullets: Scam and trap detector for listings

tools.title: Is this listing legit?
tools.subtitle: Paste a job post, get a verdict

inputs.label: Paste the listing
inputs.placeholder: Remote Data Entry, $45/hr, message us on Telegram…

tools.prompt: Assess this listing from {source}: {listing}. Give a text verdict (Legit / Caution / Likely scam / Not really remote) with a confidence level, a table (Red or green flag | Evidence in the listing | Why it matters) with at least 5 rows, a checklist of at least 5 verification actions to complete before applying or sharing any personal data, and a callout on the data and money you must never hand over in a hiring process.

tools.title: Remote-proof my application
tools.subtitle: Show you can work async

inputs.label: Paste the job description
inputs.placeholder: Senior Backend Engineer, fully remote, EMEA hours…

inputs.label: Your relevant experience
inputs.placeholder: 3 years remote at a 40-person startup, wrote our onboarding docs

tools.prompt: Match this experience: {experience} to the role: {role}. Produce a table (Requirement in the JD | Your evidence | Strength) covering every requirement, bullets of 5 resume lines that prove async communication, self-management and written clarity with numbers, a quote with a 150-word cover note that mentions time-zone fit and working hours, and a callout on anything in the JD that contradicts the profile's preferred setup.

tools.title: Camera interview prep
tools.subtitle: Video calls and async interviews
tools.prompt: Prepare the user for a '{format}' interview at {company}. Sections: a checklist of setup (lighting, audio, background, connection backup, link tested), a table (Likely question | What they're really testing | Your 30-second answer plan) with 6 remote-specific questions such as handling silence, time zones and disagreement in writing, a quote with a strong 'how do you work remotely' answer drafted from the profile, and a callout on the one mistake that sinks remote candidates.

tools.title: Plan the take-home
tools.subtitle: Scope, time-box, deliver

inputs.label: The task as given
inputs.placeholder: build a small API with tests, 4 hours suggested

tools.prompt: Plan the take-home: {task} within {hours} hours. Produce a kv (what they are grading, minimum viable deliverable, stretch items, submission format), a table (Hour block | Work | Output) that fits {hours} hours with a buffer, a checklist for the README or cover note (assumptions, trade-offs, what you'd do with more time), and a callout on when a take-home is unreasonably large and how to push back politely.

tools.title: Decode location pay
tools.subtitle: Geo bands, currency, contractor vs employee

inputs.label: The offer or range
inputs.placeholder: $95k–$120k, adjusted for Portugal, contractor via EOR

tools.prompt: Explain this remote offer: {offer} for someone in the profile location. Sections: a kv (base, likely geo-adjustment logic, contractor vs employee implications, benefits typically missing, currency and payment method), a table (Question to ask HR | Why) with 6 rows, bullets on negotiation angles specific to remote roles (equipment stipend, co-working budget, time-zone premium), and a callout that tax and employment status vary by country and need local advice.

disclaimer: General information only; employment, tax and contractor rules vary by country. Never share ID documents or bank details before verifying an employer.
